findings.observation: The final local build now recovers a first-source timeout without duplicate people, contexts, or sources; preserves uncertain speakers and forwarded evidence; resumes unresolved identity; records identity correction history; invalidates stale approval; and withdraws and restores source authority safely. The deployed site still has no usable sign-in method, and a real elapsed cross-day return has not occurred.
findings.evidence: docs/evaluations/2026-08-11-system-ui-click-acceptance-003.json; Playwright sessions ts-99-r4 and ts-99-final-003; production session ts-99-live-002.
findings.user_impact: The frozen Web candidate is coherent and recoverable for the tested synthetic workflow, but a recruiter still cannot enter the sellable service or rely on proven next-day continuity.
findings.recommendation: Deploy behind a usable authenticated pilot account, then run the same governed relationship across a real elapsed day without database repair.
findings.verification: A consented recruiter enters production, completes the loop, returns the next day to the same current state and history, and recovers from one failed capture without duplicate work.

findings.criterion: Paid value in ordinary recruiting work
findings.observation: The UI now removes substantial trust and recovery friction in the synthetic loop, but no working recruiter has compared it with their existing notes, CRM, or ATS across repeated searches or accepted an explicit price.
findings.evidence: The 94-point matrix is system-focused and synthetic; it contains no consented repeated-use field outcome or willingness-to-pay evidence.
findings.user_impact: Usability is strongly supported inside the tested scope, while recurring economic value remains a hypothesis.
findings.recommendation: Run a concierge pilot measuring relationship-reconstruction time, missed follow-up reduction, correction cost, voluntary return, and willingness to pay.
findings.verification: At least three authorized recruiters repeat the workflow in ordinary searches and choose to continue at an explicit pilot price without safety workarounds.

strengths: The capture path truthfully survives a timeout-after-commit and replays one receipt instead of creating duplicate work.
Same-name, current-versus-historical owner, unresolved identity, and wrong-person correction paths keep recruiter judgment explicit.
Source revocation immediately removes authority and restore returns evidence to review without reviving conclusions or actions.
Current understanding, exact evidence, prior versions, one action, outcome, no-action, and deletion form one calm desktop loop.
missing_evidence: Usable authenticated production entry and guarded production build parity.
A real elapsed cross-day return on the frozen build.
Repeated-use value and willingness-to-pay evidence from consented working recruiters.
open_questions: Does the workflow save enough relationship-reconstruction time over a week to earn an explicit paid-pilot commitment?
